extracted.intended_audience: researchers (e.g., cell biologists and meta-researchers) interested in participating as crowd preprint leads or reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Coordinating and participating in a crowd-based public preprint review process: groups of researchers comment on circulated preprints via a collaborative doc over a fixed period, then synthesize comments into a single public review. The guidance covers roles (lead/reviewer), timelines, commenting medium, synthesis rules, attribution, and moderation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crowd composition and expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: The ASAPbio crowd leads will coordinate ‘crowds’ of preprint reviewers – each crowd will include a group of researchers with expertise in the designated discipline who agree to provide feedback on preprints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crowds are discipline-specific (e.g., cell biology, biochemistry, infectious diseases, meta-research). Aim for ~5–8 crowd members providing comments for each preprint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency of review assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Each crowd will receive one new preprint to review every two weeks or month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practice, crowds circulate a new preprint every two weeks and crowd members are asked to contribute comments over the following 14 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commenting period duration
rubrics_metrics.description: After 14 days, the commenting period for the paper will be closed and the collective comments will be synthesized into a single report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 14-day window defines when contributors can add comments to the shared document; synthesis follows closure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commenting medium and visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Crowd members will be invited to provide comments via a collaborative Google Doc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments in the Google Doc are visible to any member of the Google group but not to the public. Crowd members can comment on the full paper or specific parts according to their interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution expectations and flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Crowd members do not have to contribute comments every week; they can choose whether to comment on the paper circulated in a specific week according to their expertise and availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation is voluntary and flexible; the program hopes that 5–8 crowd members will provide comments per preprint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthesis creation and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: A Crowd member will collect the comments on the preprint at the end of the commenting period for a paper, and generate a synthesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synthesis will consolidate comments related to different sections of the paper for ease of reading; the synthesis produces a single report to be posted as a public review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content editing and moderation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: There will not be any edits done for content, except if any concerns arise about the tone or nature of the comment, in which case, ASAPbio can decide to exclude specific comments from the synthesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ASAPbio (or crowd leads) may exclude specific comments for tone/nature concerns; otherwise content is not edited for substance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution and anonymity in public reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: For the synthesized review that will be publicly posted, we will aggregate the comments and list contributors as a list, without linking specific comments to the commenter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributors are acknowledged in the synthesized review but public reviews do not link individual comments to specific people; internal Google Doc visibility to group members remains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting and indexing of synthesized reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The collective comments will be synthesized into a single report, to be posted as a public review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews are posted at PREreview as part of their clubs initiative and those public reviews will also be listed on Sciety; synthesized reviews are posted on the preprint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role, appointment, and support for crowd leads
rubrics_metrics.description: Crowd lead applications are assessed on a rolling basis, and each lead is appointed for a 1-year term (renewable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ASAPbio will provide a guide and support for logistics; leads coordinate crowds and collect/synthesize comments; applications may be open/closed per cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope definition for crowds
rubrics_metrics.description: There will be different crowds with specific scopes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crowds have designated discipline scopes (e.g., Cell Biology, Meta-research) and activities can include converting journal clubs into preprint review clubs and creating long-term crowds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale and intended benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: The crowd preprint review approach provides a way to engage in public preprint feedback while mitigating concerns about whether the commenter feels qualified and potential vulnerability for early career researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This model gives flexibility on what comments to provide and generates public reviews that will not link the commenter’s identity to specific comments, helping develop reviewing skills and support trust in preprints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment timeline guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating as a crowd preprint reviewer is a great opportunity ... Now accepting responses for 2026 crowds; Rolling application window, but apply by February 28 for best consideration!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sign-up is rolling and participants can join at any stage, but cycles may have recommended application cutoffs for best consideration.
